forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No credible lab has declared AGI in the last 24 hours. OpenAI beefed up Codex (16 Apr) with desktop-agent powers; Anthropic's unreleased Claude Mythos Preview hits 93.9% on SWE-bench Verified but is gated under Project Glasswing. Metaculus combined forecast still pegs AGI around mid-2030 (80% CI: 2027-2043). Kalshi ~42% OpenAI-AGI-by-2030; Polymarket 9% for AGI-by-2027. Hold at 25%.
forecasts.base_rate: ~25% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi and expert surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Metaculus median AGI arrival still mid-2030 (+3pp)
Claude Mythos Preview 93.9% SWE-bench (+2pp)
OpenAI Codex upgraded to desktop agent 16 Apr (+2pp)
Anthropic at $30B ARR validates commercial demand (+2pp)
factors_down: No credible lab has declared AGI (-4pp)
key_uncertainties: What threshold of capability counts as 'AGI' for resolution
Whether Project Glasswing-class models trigger AGI claims
Timing of first autonomous R&D demonstrations

update_triggers.up: A major lab publicly declares AGI, or 3+ leading researchers endorse a specific milestone
update_triggers.down: Stall in frontier capability benchmarks, or major labs walk back timelines

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: McKinsey confirmed ~10% layoffs affecting 'a few thousand' mostly non-client-facing roles over 18-24 months; headcount down from 45k+ peak to ~40k. But implementation-led firms (Accenture, Deloitte, EY) still growing 11-12% CAGR while MBB compounds 5-6%. Global consulting revenue base still expanding. No directional shift. Hold at 18%.
forecasts.base_rate: Historical white-collar sectors rarely see 33% decline in 5-6 years absent collapse; but AI disruption is unprecedented shock
factors_up: McKinsey 10% layoffs now confirmed, not just reported (+2pp)
MBB growth slowing to 5-6% vs implementation 11-12% (+2pp)
Internal AI agents replacing junior analyst workflows (+2pp)
Consulting grad-hire postings still down meaningfully YoY (+1pp)
factors_down: Global consulting revenue base still growing (-4pp)
Big Four/Accenture continue upward revenue trajectory (-3pp)
AI-enabled advisory work is substituting, not evaporating (-2pp)
No credible scenario projecting 33% industry decline by 2030 (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether 'value' means revenue, headcount, or billable hours
How durable enterprise AI-advisory demand proves
Whether a recessionary shock coincides with AI displacement

update_triggers.up: A Big Four or MBB firm announces >20% headcount cut, or industry revenue falls YoY
update_triggers.down: Industry revenue growth re-accelerates materially, or mass recruitment returns

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Latest YouGov (12-13 April) holds Reform 24%, Con 19%, Grn 18%, Lab 17%, LD 13% — Labour remains in a four-way tie for second place, 7pp behind Reform. More in Common April MRP still projects ~324 Reform seats. No bounce since last week. Hold at 4%.
forecasts.base_rate: Incumbent parties polling 4th 3+ years out rarely recover to win most seats; base rate ~5-8%
factors_up: Three years until legal deadline for next GE (+3pp)
UK polling historically volatile — Reform could split (+2pp)
Labour still has government levers to deploy (+1pp)
Opposition fragmentation helps plurality under FPTP (+1pp)
factors_down: Labour polling 4th at 17% with no recovery trend (-4pp)
Reform consistent 24% lead across multiple pollsters (-3pp)
MRP projections show catastrophic Labour seat collapse (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Reform holds together through a full electoral cycle
Whether economy/immigration dynamics shift before GE
Who emerges as opposition leader and with what coalition

update_triggers.up: Labour polling recovers above 25% sustainably, or Reform collapses
update_triggers.down: Reform lead extends beyond 10pp, or Labour loses major by-election

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Metaculus combined forecast median still mid-2030 (80% CI 2027-2043) — the central mass sits comfortably inside the 2035 deadline. Capability milestones this week (Claude Mythos 93.9% SWE-bench, OpenAI GPT-5.4-Cyber, Codex desktop agent) reinforce trajectory. Anthropic's $30B ARR gives it commercial fuel for another decade of scaling. Hold at 73%.
forecasts.base_rate: Metaculus combined median AGI 2030 with 80% CI 2027-2043; ~70-75% falls before 2035
factors_up: Metaculus median mid-2030 well inside the 2035 window (+6pp)
Frontier benchmark saturation accelerating (+4pp)
Anthropic $30B ARR funds multi-year compute scaling (+3pp)
Labs now have autonomous coding agents in production (+2pp)

Whether AGI resolution criteria are met by agentic systems
Whether geopolitics disrupts frontier development

update_triggers.up: A major lab publicly declares AGI, or multiple experts endorse

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: G7+EU joint statement (6 April) condemned PLA's early-April three-phase exercise; Penghu live-fire drills continue. But DNI assessment still reads PRC as not planning near-term invasion and Beijing appears to prefer grey-zone coercion plus coast-guard pressure. No cross-strait escalation to kinetic action. Hold at 10%.
forecasts.base_rate: Great-power invasions during 5-year windows are historically rare; base ~5-15%
factors_up: PLA's April three-phase exercise rehearsing blockade (+3pp)
G7+EU joint condemnation shows rising alarm (+2pp)
Increased hypersonic missile deployment near strait (+2pp)
Xi's continued unification rhetoric (+1pp)
factors_down: DNI: PRC 'does not currently plan invasion' (-3pp)
Costs of blockade vs. deterrence currently too high (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether US commitment changes decisively
How Taiwanese politics evolve through 2028 election
Whether Chinese economic distress accelerates timeline

update_triggers.up: PLA announces >72hr blockade or declares crossing force posture
update_triggers.down: Beijing-Taipei dialogue resumes, or PLA tempo visibly slows

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: BoE March 2026 MPR: CPI expected close to 3.5% in March and 3.0-3.5% through Q2-Q3 2026 on Middle East energy shock. CPI was 3.0% in both January and February 2026 per ONS. Only ~8 months of prints remain before 1 Jan 2027, all with base effects working against a sub-2% reading. Hold at 1% floor.
forecasts.base_rate: Mechanical: with CPI at 3% and BoE expecting 3-3.5% through Q3, virtually no path to <2% by Dec 2026
factors_up: Oil prices could reverse sharply on Middle East ceasefire (+1pp)
Services inflation could ease faster than expected (+1pp)
GBP strengthening could import disinflation (+0.5pp)
factors_down: BoE now projecting 3-3.5% CPI into Q3 2026 (-2pp)
Only 8 months of CPI prints remain (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Trajectory of Middle East energy shock
Speed of services disinflation
How ONS handles April 2026 utility cap changes

update_triggers.up: Brent collapses below $55, or a single CPI print comes in <2.2%
update_triggers.down: Any CPI print >3.5%, or BoE further upgrades forecast

factors_up: Variety/koimoi both project $2.31-2.54B (+4pp)
Trailer >1B views (industry first) (+2pp)
Polymarket 45.5% top-2026 film (+2pp)
No Way Home comp at $1.92B (+2pp)

Whether China gets a simultaneous release
How Avengers: Doomsday affects July-Nov windowing

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Anthropic confirmed at $30B ARR (overtook OpenAI), closed $30B Series G at $380B valuation, IPO targeted October. OpenAI ~$25B ARR. Combined ~$55B in April. With three quarters of historical 2-3x annualised growth, combined $70B by Q4 2026 remains highly likely barring a material slowdown. Hold at 96%.

factors_up: Anthropic $30B ARR confirmed (+3pp)
Anthropic $30B Series G closed at $380B (+2pp)
Claude Code alone at $1B+ ARR (+1pp)
Enterprise demand still accelerating (+1pp)
factors_down: Definition of ARR vs forward bookings contested (-1pp)

How OpenAI's consumer ARR evolves post-Codex
What Q4 2026 credible report will be available by resolution

update_triggers.down: Either firm reports ARR flat or declining in H2 2026

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: OBR March 2026 forecast has real GDP per person at 1.1% a year 2026-2030 with productivity assumed to pick up to 1% medium-term and labour supply growth declining to ~0.5% by 2030. Implies trend GDP around 1.5% — right at the threshold. IMF still 1.2% (2025) / 1.4% (2026). AI productivity remains the key upside swing factor. Hold at 44%.
forecasts.base_rate: UK 10-year avg real GDP growth was 1.2% in 2010s, 1.3-1.5% trend per most official forecasts; ~40-50% chance of beating 1.5%
factors_up: OBR March 2026 medium-term productivity at 1% (+3pp)
AI productivity upside not yet priced in (+3pp)
Post-Brexit regulatory divergence optionality (+2pp)
Planning reform pipeline improving (+1pp)
factors_down: Labour supply growth slowing to ~0.5% by 2030 (-3pp)
Public debt at 95% of GDP crowds out investment (-2pp)
IFS skeptical of OBR productivity assumptions (-2pp)
Demographic ageing pulls on trend growth (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Size and timing of AI productivity dividend
Whether net migration stabilises or falls further
Whether capital investment rebounds to G7 average

update_triggers.down: Further cuts to TFP assumption, or protracted recession
